sanskrit: nābhūd ahir bhrūṇam ārad ahir adrim arasāvadhīt | viṣasya brahmaṇāmāsīt tato jīvan na mokṣase ||
english: The serpent was not as an embryo; the serpent struck the stone-cloud and rendered its venom impotent. By the brahman of the poison it came into being — from that, alive, you shall not escape.

sanskrit: uṣṭo 'hiḥ samuṣṭo *'hir nirdhīto arasaḥ kṛtaḥ | viṣasya brahmaṇāmāsīt tato jīvan na mokṣase ||
english: The serpent is scorched, the serpent is utterly scorched, rendered juiceless, made powerless. By the brahman of the poison it came into being — from that, alive, you shall not escape.

sanskrit: punar dadāmi te viṣaṃ pūrvapadyam id āritha | māṃ dadaśvān manyase mayā daṣṭo na mokṣase ||
english: I give back your venom to you — you have indeed reached your former step. You think yourself one who has bitten me; bitten by me, you shall not escape.

sanskrit: ekaśataṃ bheṣajāni teṣāṃ mātāsy oṣadhe | samudram ava gacchasi pṛthivyām adhi niṣṭhitā ||
english: One hundred and one are the remedies; of them you are the mother, O herb. You flow down to the ocean, established upon the earth.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ vedādhi bheṣajaṃ daśaśīrṣo daśajihvaḥ | yas te prathama ādade śaṃ śvāvanta oṣadhe yam adād vīrayug bhiṣak ||
english: In her I know the remedy: the ten-headed, ten-tongued one. He who first gathered you — may he fare well, O herb; and he to whom the heroic physician gave you — may he be well.

sanskrit: punaś cakṣuḥ punaḥ prāṇaḥ punar āyur na āgamat | niṣ ṭvākaraṃ niṣkṛtyā niṣ ṭvā niṣkṛtyākaram ||
english: May sight return again, may breath return again, may life's span return again to us. I have extracted you by the counter-rite; by the counter-rite I have extracted you.

sanskrit: muñcāmi tvā śapathyād atho varuṇyād uta | atho yamasya paḍvīśād viśvasmād devakilbiṣāt ||
english: I release you from the bond of the curse, and also from that which belongs to Varuṇa; and from the foot-fetter of Yama, from every transgression against the gods.

sanskrit: saṃ te śīrṣṇaḥ kapālāni hṛdayasya ca yo viduḥ | udyan sūrya ādityo aṅgadyotam anīnaśat ||
english: Well joined are the skull-plates of your head and of your heart — those who know them. The rising sun, Āditya, has caused the body's radiance to shine forth.

sanskrit: himavataḥ pra sravatha sindhau samaha saṅgamaḥ | tā āpaḥ sarvāḥ saṅgatya cakṣuḥ prāṇaṃ ca dhatta naḥ ||
english: Flow forth from Himavat; your confluence is in the Sindhu. Let all those waters, gathering together, bestow sight and breath upon us.

sanskrit: hastivarcasaṃ prathatāṃ bṛhad yaśo adityā yat tanvaḥ saṃbabhūva | tat sarve savitur mahyam etad viśve devāso aditiḥ sajoṣāḥ ||
english: May the elephant-splendour spread wide, the great glory that arose from the body of Aditi. All of that — this which is Savitṛ's — let all the gods together with Aditi grant to me.

sanskrit: mitraś ca varuṇaś ca- -indro rudraś ca vedhatu | devāso viśvadhāyasas tena māñjantu varcasā ||
english: Let Mitra and Varuṇa, and Indra and Rudra fashion it. Let the gods, sustainers of all, anoint me with that splendour.

sanskrit: yat te varco jātavedo bṛhad bhavaty āhute | tena mām adya varcasā agne varcasvinaṃ kṛdhi ||
english: That great radiance of yours, O Jātavedas, which blazes up when you are invoked — with that radiance today, O Agni, make me full of splendour.

sanskrit: yena hastī varcasā saṃbabhūva yena rājā manuṣyeṣv antaḥ | yena devā jyotiṣā dyām udāyan tena māgne varcasā saṃ sṛjeha ||
english: By that splendour whereby the elephant came into being, whereby the king stands foremost among men, whereby the gods ascended heaven with their light — with that splendour, O Agni, unite me here.

sanskrit: yāvad varcaḥ sūryasya- -asurasya ca hastinaḥ | tāvan me aśvinā varcaḥ kṛṇutaṃ puṣkarasrajā ||
english: As great as is the splendour of the sun and of the mighty elephant — that much splendour, O you two Aśvins garlanded with lotus-wreaths, create for me.

sanskrit: yāvac catasraḥ pradiśaś cakṣur yāvat samaśnute | tāvat sam aitv indriyaṃ mayi tad dhastivarcasam ||
english: As far as the four cardinal directions, as far as the eye reaches in its range — let that vital power, that elephant-splendour, gather itself entirely within me.
